language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I'm Nita! I live on Cocos Island in the Indian Ocean.

Everyday when I look up at the sky, I see the sun. When the sun looks like it is going down, it isn't really going down. It's an illusion! It's the earth that is spinning, and that's why it looks like the sun is moving. I've learned that the earth is spinning around its axis and it makes exactly one complete spin every day.
At night when the sun sets, we see the earth spinning away from the sun. In the morning when the sun rises, earth is spinning towards the sun so it becomes lighter and lighter.
Hi! Do you see how the earth is spinning around its axis? Can you guess how long it takes the earth to make one full spin?
It takes the earth 24 hours or one full day to spin once around its axis. This is fun! Help me as I learn about the earth, sun and moon!

Since the earth rotates around its own axis and around the sun, the sun always comes up and goes down in the same place. Did you know they call Japan "the land of the rising sun"?  This is because Japan is to the east of China and Europe, and the sun gets up every morning....in the east! Use this information to answer the following questions.
